# Data schemas (generated)

<!-- Generated by `uv run ccil schema docs`; edit the specs in src/ccil/schema/, not this file. -->

## `ccil.trajectories` 1.0

An episode is T frames. Frame t has one entry per observation modality and an action; a transition is (frame t, action t, frame t+1), identified by (episode_id, t) for t <= T-2. Every action frame must be finite because policies also train on the final (observation, action) pair.

### Episode

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `episode_id` | `str` | Unique, non-empty identifier of the episode. |
| `observations` | `dict[str, array]` | Named modalities matching state, state.<name>, or image.<camera>. |
| `actions` | `array` | Action applied at each frame. |
| `terminated` | `bool` | True if the episode ended in a terminal state; False if it was truncated. |
| `timestamps` | `array \| None` | Frame times; strictly increasing. Given for every episode or none. |
| `task` | `str \| None` | Task identifier or instruction. |
| `action_chunks` | `array \| None` | action_chunks[t, k] is the action intended at frame t + k. Given for every episode or none, with one K. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | `array \| None` | True exactly where t + k < T; required with action_chunks. A chunk never crosses the episode end. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observations[state*]` | float | (T, D) | task-defined | yes | Low-dimensional state per frame; a modality named state or state.<name>. |
| `observations[image*]` | uint8 | (T, H, W, C) | pixel intensity 0-255 | yes | Camera frames per frame; a modality named image.<camera>, C in {1, 3, 4}. |
| `actions` | float | (T, A) | task-defined | yes | Action applied at each frame. |
| `timestamps` | float | (T,) | seconds | no | Frame times; strictly increasing. Given for every episode or none. |
| `action_chunks` | float | (T, K, A) | task-defined | no | action_chunks[t, k] is the action intended at frame t + k. Given for every episode or none, with one K. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | bool | (T, K) | - | no | True exactly where t + k < T; required with action_chunks. A chunk never crosses the episode end. |

Modality names match `^(state|image)(\.[a-z0-9_]+)?$`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `actions`, `episode_ids`, `episode_lengths`, `terminated`, and `obs/<modality>` per modality. Optional: `action_chunk_mask`, `action_chunks`, `task`, `task_present`, `timestamps`. Per-frame arrays are concatenated across episodes in `episode_ids` order and split by `episode_lengths`.

## `ccil.candidates` 2.3

One row per attempted candidate, accepted or rejected. A row is accepted exactly when it carries no rejection reason; a rejected row may carry several independent reasons. Source identity (episode_id, frame), measurements, and a training weight are required on every row, and the file records the run, seed, generator, input hashes (always including the transition model), and weighting that produced it, so an accepted label can be traced and replayed from the candidate file alone.  Reason columns are the built-in codes, whose meanings are fixed, and namespaced extension codes <namespace>.<reason> that a method's own validators declare (the ccil namespace is reserved). Built-ins come first in their canonical order, then extensions sorted. A consumer that does not know an extension's namespace still treats the row as rejected: accepted is True exactly when no column, built-in or extension, rejects the row.  2.0 made weight, seed, inputs, and weighting required (1.0 had none of them). 2.1 added extension reason codes; a file declares 2.1 only when it uses one, so files with built-in reasons alone stay 2.0. 2.2 added the optional measurement_specs, the definition, norm, and units of every measurement, and the generator's full params; a file declares 2.2 only when it carries specs. 2.3 added optional action chunks (action_chunks, action_chunk_mask, and the meta action_chunk_spec); a file declares 2.3 only when it carries chunks, and lists the arrays in optional_fields so 2.2 readers ignore them.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `str` | Identifier of the run that produced the candidates. |
| `generator` | `dict` | name, version, and params_hash of the generator; optionally params, its full parameters. |
| `seed` | `int` | Seed the generator drew its randomness from. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex) of each input by name; always includes transition_model, the model checkpoint the labels came from. |
| `weighting` | `dict` | name, version, and params of the weighting that produced weight. |
| `measurement_specs` | `dict \| None` | Optional (2.2): for every measurement name, its definition, norm (or null), and units. |
| `action_chunk_spec` | `dict \| None` | Optional (2.3), with action chunks: chunk_size, alignment, guarantee, and truncation; requires the measurement chunk_target_frame. |
| `reason_codes` | `tuple[str]` | Column labels of reasons, distinct and in canonical order: built-ins ['non_finite', 'out_of_support', 'generation_failed', 'action_out_of_bounds'] first, then extension codes <namespace>.<reason> sorted. |
| `observations` | `dict[str, array (N, ...)]` | Candidate observation per modality: a trajectory modality, or latent.<name> for labels in a learned representation. |
| `target_observations` | `dict[str, array (N, ...)]` | Observation the candidate action should reach, per modality. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_episode_id` | str | (N,) | - | yes | Episode the candidate perturbs. |
| `source_frame` | int | (N,) | frames | yes | Transition index t in the source episode (t <= T-2). |
| `actions` | float | (N, A) | task-defined | yes | Candidate action. |
| `accepted` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | True exactly when the row has no rejection reason. |
| `reasons` | bool | (N, R) | - | yes | reasons[i, r] is True when reason_codes[r] rejects row i. |
| `measurements[name]` | float | (N,) | per measurement | yes | Validity measurements (e.g. distance, residual); NaN allowed only on rejected rows. |
| `weight` | float | (N,) | - | yes | Training weight; finite and >= 0 on accepted rows, 0 on rejected rows. |
| `action_chunks` | float | (N, K, A) | task-defined | no | Optional (2.3): position 0 is the label action; position k >= 1 is the source episode's action at chunk_target_frame + k - 1. Only position 0 carries the label's one-step claim. |
| `action_chunk_mask` | bool | (N, K) | - | no | Optional (2.3): True exactly at positions inside the source episode; never padded. |

Candidate modality names match `^(?:(state|image)(\.[a-z0-9_]+)?|latent\.[a-z0-9_]+)$`.

Built-in reason codes: `non_finite`, `out_of_support`, `generation_failed`, `action_out_of_bounds`. Extension codes match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`; reserved namespaces: `ccil`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `accepted`, `actions`, `reasons`, `source_episode_id`, `source_frame`, `weight`, plus `obs/<modality>`, `target/<modality>`, and `meas/<name>`. Optional: `action_chunk_mask`, `action_chunks`. `meta` holds `action_chunk_spec`, `generator`, `inputs`, `measurement_specs`, `reason_codes`, `run_id`, `seed`, `weighting`.

## `ccil.certificates` 1.0

One row per candidate row of a ccil.candidates file, in the same order, with the source identity repeated for joining; the candidates file is never modified. A row records the terms its profile used (every term the descriptor declares is persisted), model_error_value and total_error_value, a classification, is_upper_bound (true exactly for certified, conditional, and calibrated rows), whether the label lies in the profile's neighborhood, and the admissible and selected masks with independent certificate reasons. The file records the profile descriptor (form, terms, constants with their sources and provenance, the demonstration residual's source, whether model terms are evaluated with an error bound, neighborhood, coordinates and scales, derived units, assumptions), the admission policy, the selection, the SHA-256 of every input (always the candidates, dataset, and transition model), and the identity of the representation and transition model. Training uses candidate.accepted & admissible & selected.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `descriptor` | `dict` | profile, version, form (additive, direct, score), terms {name: {definition, units, required}}, constants {role: {value, source, maps, rationale, provenance}}, neighborhood {state, action} (null = unbounded), coordinates {modality, state_dim, action_dim, state_scale, action_scale}, model_evaluation (bounded: the model terms are upper bounds; assumed_exact: they assume exact evaluation), demonstration {source, value, rationale, provenance} for profiles that add the demonstration residual, units, norms, assumptions. |
| `admission` | `dict` | mode ['upper_bound', 'score'] and threshold (null or finite >= 0) on total_error_value. |
| `selection` | `dict` | quantile (null or in (0, 1]) and the resulting threshold (null when no quantile or no eligible row). |
| `candidates_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the candidates file. |
| `inputs` | `dict[str, str]` | SHA-256 of each input by name; always ['candidates', 'dataset', 'transition_model']. |
| `components` | `dict` | representation {kind, version, modality} and transition_model {kind, version}. |
| `classification_codes` | `list[str]` | Exactly ['certified', 'conditional', 'calibrated', 'empirical', 'unsupported']. |
| `reason_codes` | `list[str]` | Exactly ['certificate.unsupported', 'certificate.not_upper_bound', 'certificate.exceeds_threshold', 'certificate.not_selected']. |

### Arrays

| Field | Kind | Shape | Units | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_episode_id` | str | (N,) | - | yes | Episode of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `source_frame` | int | (N,) | frames | yes | Transition index of the candidate row; equals the candidates file's. |
| `term/<name>` | float | (N,) | per descriptor.terms | yes | Every term the descriptor declares; NaN allowed only where the row is unsupported or the term is not required. |
| `model_error_value` | float | (N,) | error | yes | Additive profiles: the bound on ||f(q) - f_hat(q)||. NaN for direct and score profiles. |
| `total_error_value` | float | (N,) | error | yes | The bound (bound classifications) or score (empirical) on ||T(q) - y||; finite and >= 0 unless unsupported. |
| `classification` | int | (N,) | - | yes | Index into classification_codes. |
| `is_upper_bound` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | True exactly for certified, conditional, and calibrated rows. |
| `in_neighborhood` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | The label lies in the profile's neighborhood. |
| `admissible` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | Passes the admission policy; never set on unsupported rows. |
| `selected` | bool | (N,) | - | yes | Budget selection; with a quantile, a subset of accepted & admissible rows, otherwise every row. |
| `reasons` | bool | (N, R) | - | yes | reasons[i, r] is True when reason_codes[r] applies to row i. |

Classifications: `certified`, `conditional`, `calibrated`, `empirical`, `unsupported`; bounds: `certified`, `conditional`, `calibrated`. Reason codes, in column order: `certificate.unsupported`, `certificate.not_upper_bound`, `certificate.exceeds_threshold`, `certificate.not_selected`. Global terms, persisted by every profile: `state_displacement`, `action_displacement`, `anchor_model_error`, `solver_error`. Constant sources: `analytic_bound`, `model_bound`, `declared`.

### File layout (.npz)

Required: `admissible`, `classification`, `in_neighborhood`, `is_upper_bound`, `model_error_value`, `reasons`, `selected`, `source_episode_id`, `source_frame`, `total_error_value`, and `term/<name>` for exactly the descriptor's terms. `meta` holds `admission`, `candidates_sha256`, `components`, `descriptor`, `inputs`, `selection`, `classification_codes`, and `reason_codes`; no other array or meta field is accepted.

## Compatibility

Files are written atomically and read with allow_pickle=False. `meta` is a JSON string with schema, version "MAJOR.MINOR", and optional_fields. A file that cannot be decoded (not an archive, truncated, pickled arrays, non-JSON or mistyped meta, inconsistent array layout) raises SchemaError, never a raw decoding error. Compatibility: a minor version only adds optional fields; a reader accepts its own major version, ignores ext/<name> keys, ignores unknown keys only when the file declares them optional (written by a newer minor), and rejects anything else.
